title: 24.8 A 12GS/s 9b 16× Time-Interleaved SAR ADC in 16nm FinFET
problem: RF direct sampling and phased-array applications require high-speed ADCs (>GS/s) with both high sample rate and high SNDR (>45dB), but existing designs often require multiple supply domains or complex integration schemes.
motivation: Emerging RF direct sampling and digital phased-array beamforming require medium-resolution high-speed ADCs to simultaneously achieve throughput and RF performance without complicating system integration.
method: The chip uses 16 parallel SAR ADC channels (successive approximation converters that build up each measurement bit by bit) working in interleaved time slices to reach 12 billion samples per second. It's manufactured in 16nm FinFET technology (a modern process that densely packs transistors), and instead of requiring custom voltage levels, it runs on just two standard supplies—1.8V and 0.8V—which simplifies integration into larger systems while keeping the circuit small and power-efficient.
key_novelty: The key innovation is using standard power supply voltages from the chip's manufacturing process rather than custom ones, which simplifies integration into larger transceiver systems while maintaining a 48.1dB SNDR (signal-to-noise and distortion ratio).
contributions: Integration-friendly with standard 1.8V/0.8V supplies avoiding complex multi-domain design
baselines: high-SNDR SAR ADCs with 3+ supply domains
primary_theme: integration-friendly high-speed SAR ADC for RF direct sampling
